newsitem.title: USA: Pa. court to take up school funding Monday - paper.
newsitem.headline: Pa. court to take up school funding Monday - paper.

text.p: A long-delayed court case challenging Pennsylvania's system of public school funding is set to begin Monday in Commonwealth Court, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Monday.
The case, brought by the Pennsylvania Association of Rural and Small Schools, or PARSS, argues that spending among rich and poor districts in the state should be equalized.
Pennsylvania is the latest in a string of states that have grappled with lawsuits challenging property taxes as an inherently unfair method of financing public education.

Rural schools in Pennsylvania typically spend far below the state average of $6,400 per pupil, and theoretically have the most to gain from reform. But urban and suburban districts have also called for a new system.
Last year, the judge in the case gave Gov Tom Ridge the option of settling out of court with PARSS, which was proposing the elimination of property taxes as the method of funding. Ridge declined.
